exercise.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercise.equipment: dumbbell (pair) + upright bench with back support
exercise.one_line_summary: Sitting tall against a near-upright back pad, press two dumbbells from ear height straight up until the arms are almost straight over the shoulders, then lower them slowly. Front shoulder leads; side shoulder and triceps help.
exercise.evidence_note: Muscle rows are grade A/B: two EMG studies on the seated dumbbell press itself (S2, S4) and three on close variants (S1, S3, S5). Joint angles are grade C: no study measured the joint angles of the seated dumbbell press, so they come from the NSCA technique text, ACE, and shoulder-motion research. Shoulder-girdle motion is grade B: measured in unloaded arm raising in vivo (S8 Ludewig 2009, S10 McClure 2001 bone pins, S11 Inman 1944), not in a loaded press. v7 kept the shoulder blade and collarbone still; the owner rejected it (30 Oct 2026) because the armpit and shoulder skin folded and seemed to twist overhead. From v8 the collarbone and shoulder blade move with the arm (scapulohumeral rhythm). LIMITS of this body: the rig has one collarbone bone and one shoulder-blade bone (shoulder01, starting mid-collarbone), so the shoulder blade's backward tilt (~20-30 deg, S8/S10) and outward turn are not modelled and the blade itself never shows under the skin; armpit skin still stretches ~2x overhead, so its painted grooves are softened there (skin.calm_armpits).

setup.why: A near-upright back support keeps the trunk still and the press vertical. Sitting with support lets people lift ~10 % more than standing (S2) and stops the lower back arching.

setup.target: Hips on the seat, back against the pad, both feet flat on the floor
setup.tolerance: No contact point lifts at any frame

setup.target: Closed grip, palms facing forward, handles in line left to right
setup.tolerance: Handles may turn in up to ~20 degrees
setup.why: The classic version; a neutral or semi-neutral grip is a separate variation.

setup.target: Dumbbells at ear height, upper arms a little below level, forearms vertical
setup.tolerance: Handles between shoulder and top-of-head height
setup.why: Lowering to shoulder level (the widest range) raised activity in every shoulder muscle measured versus a shorter range (S4).

setup.target: Elbows about 20 degrees forward of the body's side line
setup.why: Elbows slightly forward (toward the shoulder blade's own plane) is the cue in NSCA/ACE and keeps the shoulder joint comfortable; elbows pulled behind the body line is a listed fault.

setup.target: Straight wrist, stacked over the elbow
setup.why: A bent-back wrist under load is a listed fault.

movement.measure: elev: angle between the upper arm and the side of the torso, 0 = arm hanging
movement.start: bottom: ~75 deg (upper arm a little below level)
movement.path: One smooth sweep up and back down

movement.measure: plane: 0 = straight out to the side, +90 = straight forward

movement.path: Stays vertical: the hand stays over the elbow

movement.joint: upper-arm roll (turn of the upper arm about its own length)
movement.measure: twist of the upper-arm bone vs rest, degrees
movement.path: Smooth; changes by under ~15 deg over the rep

movement.measure: bend back/forward and twist vs rest
handle front/back position vs the shoulder joint, side view
movement.start: bottom: in front of the shoulder (elbows forward)
movement.path: Straight up with a slight drift back to finish over the shoulders
movement.tolerance: top within ~5 cm of the shoulder joint

movement.path: Hands come slightly together as the arms straighten

movement.measure: shoulder-blade upward turn, collarbone lift and draw-back, vs arm raise
movement.start: bottom (arm 75 deg): blade turned up ~15 deg, collarbone up ~3 deg, back ~5 deg
movement.end: top (arm 172 deg): blade turned up ~50 deg, collarbone up ~11 deg, back ~16 deg
movement.path: Still below ~30 deg of arm raise, then the shoulder blade turns upward ~0.4 deg per deg of arm raise (about 1 deg per 2-2.5 deg: glenohumeral:scapulothoracic 2:1 Inman, 2.2:1 Ludewig scapular plane, 1.7:1 McClure) to ~50 deg overhead (McClure 50 +-5; Ludewig 11->50); the collarbone lifts ~6-11 deg (Ludewig +6, McClure ~2->13; Inman's older radiographs ~30) and draws back ~16 deg (Ludewig 23->39). The clip uses: blade 0.4 deg/deg past 30 deg (cap 50), collarbone lift 0.08 deg/deg (cap 11), draw-back 0.12 deg/deg (cap 16), eased in over 15 deg. Not modelled: blade backward tilt ~20-30 deg and collarbone spin ~31 deg (no bone for them).
movement.tolerance: blade 40-60 deg at the top; shoulder joint rises 2-5 cm with the girdle (part of the normal rhythm), no extra shrug

movement.measure: lean and contact with the pad and seat

muscles.emg: 33.3 % MVIC, the highest of 4 exercises (shoulder press, 60 % 1RM) [S1]. Seated dumbbell ~11 % above seated barbell [S2]. Highest-activity deltoid head in front presses [S3, S5].
muscles.role: The muscle this exercise is for: it raises the arm forward and up. Library primary; top deltoid EMG in every study.
muscles.surface: Front of the shoulder cap: from the outer third of the collarbone down over the front of the shoulder to the deltoid notch on the outer upper arm; inner edge is the groove against the upper chest.

muscles.emg: 27.9 % MVIC (~84 % of the front shoulder) [S1]; seated ~15 % below standing dumbbell [S2]; rises with full range [S4].
muscles.role: Lifts the arm out to the side; clearly working throughout.
muscles.surface: Outer point of the shoulder cap, from the acromion down to the deltoid notch.

muscles.emg: Named working muscle in all press studies; standing barbell ~39 % above dumbbell [S2]; rises in the top half as the elbow straightens [S4].
muscles.role: Straightens the elbow to finish the press.
muscles.surface: Back of the upper arm from the shoulder to the elbow.

muscles.emg: Active with the shoulder blade's upward turn; rises with the widest range [S4]; no difference between front press types [S3].
muscles.role: Turns the shoulder blade upward with serratus; not the target (a shorter range is even used to reduce it [S4]).
muscles.surface: Top of the shoulders between neck and shoulder point.

muscles.emg: Some activity in front presses, higher in front than back barbell press [S3].
muscles.role: Helps raise the arm forward early in the lift; small.
muscles.surface: Upper third of the chest below the collarbone.

muscles.role: Turns the shoulder blade upward with the trapezius as the arm goes overhead.
muscles.surface: Side of the ribcage under the armpit.

muscles.role: Holds the ball of the shoulder in its socket; supraspinatus helps start the lift.

muscles.emg: Lower when seated with support than standing.
muscles.role: Keeps the trunk still against the pad.
muscles.surface: Front and sides of the trunk.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hips slide forward, chest leans back off the pad
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a steep incline press and loads the lower back.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Shoulders rise to the ears at the top
mistakes.why_it_matters: Shifts work to the upper trapezius.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows pulled back flat in line with or behind the torso at the bottom
mistakes.why_it_matters: Puts the shoulder in an uncomfortable position under load.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Dumbbells stop well above the head
mistakes.why_it_matters: Less activity in every shoulder muscle than the full range.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knuckles point back, dumbbell behind the forearm
mistakes.why_it_matters: Strains the wrist; load no longer stacked over the elbow.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Plates hit together over the head

mistakes.why_it_matters: Controlled lowering is the standard tempo.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. (2020). Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14.
sources.what_it_gave: 13 trained men, 60 % 1RM: shoulder press front delt 33.3, middle 27.9, rear 11.4 % MVIC; front delt highest of 4 exercises.

sources.citation: Saeterbakken AH, Fimland MS (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831.
sources.what_it_gave: 15 men, 80 % 1RM, seated/standing x barbell/dumbbell: seated dumbbell front delt ~11 % above seated barbell; seated 1RM ~10 % above standing; triceps higher with barbell.

sources.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, et al. (2022). Front vs back and barbell vs machine overhead press: an electromyographic analysis and implications for resistance training. Front Physiol 13:825880.
sources.what_it_gave: 8 bodybuilders: deltoids, upper trapezius, pec major and triceps all active; front press favours pec more than back press; trapezius equal.

sources.citation: Paoli A, Marcolin G, Petrone N (2010). Influence of different ranges of motion on selective recruitment of shoulder muscles in the sitting military press: an electromyographic study. J Strength Cond Res 24(6):1578-1583.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated dumbbell press at 3 ranges: the widest range raised activity of all 8 muscles; shorter range lowers trapezius.

sources.citation: Kohler JM, Flanagan SP, Whiting WC (2010). Muscle activation patterns while lifting stable and unstable loads on stable and unstable surfaces. J Strength Cond Res 24(2):313-321.
sources.what_it_gave: Shoulder press barbell vs dumbbell: front deltoid the main mover in all conditions.

sources.citation: Haff GG, Triplett NT, eds. (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. NSCA / Human Kinetics. Ch. 15, seated dumbbell shoulder press.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated five-point position, pronated grip, start at shoulder/ear level with forearms vertical, press to full elbow extension, controlled lowering.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: seated shoulder press.
sources.what_it_gave: Back supported, elbows slightly forward, no arching, no shrug, controlled tempo.

sources.citation: Ludewig PM, Phadke V, Braman JP, et al. (2009). Motion of the shoulder complex during multiplanar humeral elevation. J Bone Joint Surg Am 91(2):378-389.
sources.what_it_gave: 12 subjects, bone pins: over full arm raising the collarbone lifted 11->17 deg (+6), drew back 23->39 deg (+16), spun back 31 deg; the shoulder blade turned upward 11->50 deg (~40) and tilted back 21 deg; glenohumeral:scapulothoracic rhythm 2.1-2.4:1.

sources.citation: Drake RL, Vogl AW, Mitchell AWM (2019). Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. Elsevier.
sources.what_it_gave: Muscle borders and actions for the skin masks.

sources.citation: McClure PW, Michener LA, Sennett BJ, Karduna AR (2001). Direct 3-dimensional measurement of scapular kinematics during dynamic movements in vivo. J Shoulder Elbow Surg 10(3):269-277.
sources.what_it_gave: 8 volunteers, bone pins in the shoulder blade: scapular-plane raise turned the blade upward 50 +-5 deg, tilted it back 30 deg, turned it out 24 deg; glenohumeral:scapulothoracic 1.7:1; collarbone lift ~2->13 deg, draw-back ~18->40 deg (Fig. 3).

sources.citation: Inman VT, Saunders JB, Abbott LC (1944). Observations on the function of the shoulder joint. J Bone Joint Surg 26(1):1-30.
sources.what_it_gave: Classic 2:1 glenohumeral to scapular rhythm over the full raise (blade ~60 deg of 180); the blade is fairly still in the first ~30 deg (setting phase).
